digest_over: Every regular file under `bundle`, in ascending order of its bundle-relative POSIX path compared as UTF-8 bytes, as the lines `<sha256 hex of the file's bytes>  <path>\n`, themselves hashed with sha256. The sort is explicit so the answer does not depend on the order a filesystem walk returns; the path is in the digest beside the content so a rename moves it; the hex digest is fixed-width and the separator is literal, so a rename and an edit cannot cancel. Reproducible without this repository's code: `cd <bundle> && find . -type f | sed 's|^\./||' | LC_ALL=C sort | tr '\n' '\0' | xargs -0 sha256sum | sha256sum`.
build_command: none ran here. `dist/schemas/3.2.8/` is a COMMITTED release artifact of the upstream repository, produced by upstream's own release run (`npm run build:schemas -- --release` at package version 3.2.8, on the `3.2.x` maintenance line) and checked in. The commit above is where the artifact is READ, not where it was built. Unlike `schemas/cache/3.2`, the version string pins this state as well as the sha does: `package.json` at this commit reads `3.2.8` and `--release` writes `dist/schemas/$(version)`, so a local `--release` build at this checkout would write to this same path.

The artifact itself first appears one commit earlier, at `71121dff2b326c310c90c27ac037b75c49943410` "Version Packages", which is an ancestor of the tag; the two carry the IDENTICAL tree for this path (`git rev-parse <rev>:dist/schemas/3.2.8` is `927add24d4042c4bb18b719956044ee7837e276f` at both), and no commit between the tag and upstream's HEAD at the time of measurement (`a00249e6a7d58c4e549948547b290007d4e54645`, 2026-11-06) touches `dist/schemas/3.2.8` at all. The TAG is recorded because it is the release's own identity and the artifact is a release artifact; the "Version Packages" sha is recorded here because it is where a reader with a shallow clone of that one commit finds the same bytes.
the_fork_does_not_carry_this_artifact: `https://github.com/KonstantinMirin/adcp.git` -- the fork `schemas/cache/3.2` and `schemas/cache/3.3` are pinned to, cloned at /srv/ws/adcp-upstream -- CANNOT ground this bundle: `git ls-tree origin/main dist/schemas/` on it tops out at `dist/schemas/3.2.7`, and its `main` is `c34931a08` whose `package.json` reads `3.3.0-beta.0`. 3.2.8 was released on upstream's `3.2.x` maintenance line and the fork's `main` has not taken the forward-merge. So this record names the upstream OF RECORD as its repository where the other two name the fork, and that is a fact about where the bytes are and not a change of convention.
vendor_command:
git -C <upstream> archive 6ed4b25e261f54d6b106938d0724757bea9dc5fc dist/schemas/3.2.8 | tar -x -C <tmp> && python3 -c 'import json,pathlib,sys
src,dst=map(pathlib.Path,sys.argv[1:3])
strip=lambda o:{k:strip(v) for k,v in o.items() if k!="$id"} if isinstance(o,dict) else [strip(v) for v in o] if isinstance(o,list) else o
for p in sorted(src.rglob("*.json")):
    q=dst/p.relative_to(src); q.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
    q.write_text(json.dumps(strip(json.loads(p.read_bytes())),indent=2))' <tmp>/dist/schemas/3.2.8 schemas/cache/3.2.8
vendor_transform: `schemas/cache/3.2`'s transform, applied verbatim and for its reason rather than for symmetry: every `$id` key is removed RECURSIVELY -- not only the root one -- and each document is re-serialised by Python `json.dumps(obj, indent=2)`, whose defaults escape every non-ASCII codepoint and write no trailing newline. The transform is the SAME as 3.2's because the comparison this bundle exists for is against 3.2, and a bundle vendored by `schemas/cache/3.3`'s byte copy would differ from 3.2 in the transform as well as in the release -- which would make every three-way figure read a mixture of two questions. Measured on the committed directory: 0 of 1,625 files carry a `$id` key, 0 of 1,625 hold a byte outside ASCII, and 0 of 1,625 end in a newline. This bundle is therefore NOT byte-identical to any upstream artifact and cannot be: it is a re-serialisation of one, and the transform is part of its identity.

reproduction.why_there_are_none_where_3_2_has_one: `schemas/cache/3.2` excepts `manifest.json` because its `generated_at` is wall-clock and the copy it was vendored from was read 29.5 s after the committed artifact's stamp -- so that bundle is not reproducible from the committed bytes. This bundle was vendored DIRECTLY from the committed artifact at the sha above, so the wall-clock fields are the artifact's own and the transform is deterministic: re-running `vendor_command` reproduces all 1,625 documents. The exception list is therefore empty because there is nothing to except, not because the claim was weakened -- and the claim is the stronger of the two.
reproduction.nearest_rejected_candidates: `dist/schemas/3.2.1` through `3.2.7` each hold exactly 1,625 documents at exactly these 1,625 paths. They fail on `$ref` values, which carry the version string: every one of this bundle's 3,795 resolving absolute references is spelled `https://adcontextprotocol.org/schemas/3.2.8/<path>`, so no other 3.2.x artifact reproduces a referencing document. The published site agrees the version is the current one: `https://adcontextprotocol.org/schemas/latest.json` reads `latest_stable: 3.2.8` and `https://adcontextprotocol.org/schemas/index.json` aliases `v3`, `v3.2` and `latest_by_major.3` to it.

Four 3.2.x releases landed between `schemas/cache/3.2`'s artifact (3.2.4, 2026-10-12) and this one (3.2.8, 2026-10-28) and NONE of them fixed any of the 18 defects: the five documents #8525 asks for are still absent and the thirteen `title` keywords #8735 asks for are still unstated. So five 3.3 releases (beta.0 through beta.4) and four 3.2.x releases fixed NONE of the 18, and the real distinction is between the three bundles that are upstream's artifacts and the one bundle we built from our own ask. **AND `adcp-client-python-82m.60`'s per-entry `bundles` key loses its subject with it**: it was filed on the strength of the per-line reading corrected here, and with 3.3.0-beta.4 pinned no entry has a genuine per-bundle defect left to scope.
